To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified two distinct G. bulloids genotypes with either warm or cold temperature preferences in the Arabian Sea and that we found genotype-specific geochemical signatures in the Mg/Ca and the δ18O values of these foraminifera.

the presence of cryptic genotypes within the planktonic foram G. bulloids may influence geochemical records of this species in the Arabian Sea and potentially in other ocean regions with strong environmental gradients.
the geochemical signals of planktonic forminifera can be significantly influenced by genotype-specific biological controls.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of fossil G. bulloids as an oceanic proxy should be done with caution and that the presence of cryptic genetic variants within a morphologically defined species may lead to misinterpretation of the paleoenvironment.
the presence of distinct genotypes within morphospecies can have significant impacts on geochemical signals of fossil assemblages and may lead to erroneous paleoceanographic reconstructions.
it is essential to understand the biological controls on the geochemistry of fossil assemblages to avoid misinterpretation of paleoclimate records.
